answer: Every new agent wallet must post a costly, publicly checkable registration stamp that older agents counter-sign, so an identity works only after collecting endorsements from holders with real history. This acts as a beacon, showing peers how deep each endorsement graph runs before trust is granted. A forger spinning up a thousand wallets pays compute and collateral per identity and cannot fake the anchor of reputation that time alone earns. Each proven forgery also sends a ripple through the graph, quarantining cluster peers, so flooding costs more than joining honestly.
